title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Arjun Patel
description: Context: Private deployments require a consistent terraform state layout across GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking to support cross-account upgrades and easier drift remediation. Motivation: We have multiple private customers and on-prem installs with divergent state layouts which complicate upgrades and automated tooling; this PR unifies state layout across modules and provides a one-time migration path. Summary: - Restructure module state keys and move per-cluster resources under unified namespaced state entries. - Introduce state migration helper script (tfstate-migrate) and a documented plan for live migrations. - Rework gpu_node_pool module to use a common node pool naming scheme, decouple autoscaling IAM policies, and surface required inputs for private environments. - Consolidate networking outputs and add reverse-lookup outputs used by private installer. Migration plan: 1) Run terraform plan in a separate staging workspace to validate changes for the customer state. 2) Run included tfstate-migrate with --dry-run and review produced mapping. 3) Apply migration (writes a new state file) and run terraform apply against the updated workspace. 4) Rollout gradual node pool replacements with canary pools if needed. Rollback: instructions included in docs/terraform/private/migration.md; tfstate-migrate keeps a backup of the original state and will refuse to run if backup cannot be created. Testing: terratest suite added for module-level changes, e2e smoke tests against a test VPC, and CI plan checks to verify no unintended deletions. References: ENG-8743, INF-1291. Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about resource renaming to avoid downtime; most renames are handled as state moves only.
